title: Half in… half out.
paragraphs: Half in… half out.
That’s the most dangerous place to be.

Not fully lost.
Not fully surrendered.
Just… comfortable.

And if we’re honest?
That poster isn’t exposing them.
It’s exposing us.

Because modern-day lukewarm Christianity doesn’t look rebellious.
It looks like a normal Sunday.

Hands raised.
Lyrics sung.
Tears maybe.

But Monday comes…
and nothing changes.
Jesus spoke directly to this in Book of Revelation 3:15–16:
“I know your deeds, that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were either one or the other! So, because you are lukewarm—neither hot nor cold—I am about to spit you out of my mouth.”
Let that sit.

He didn’t say, “I’m disappointed.”
He said, “I will reject.”
Why?
Because lukewarm faith pretends intimacy without surrender.

It’s proximity without transformation.
Noise without obedience.
Religion without repentance.

You attend church… but avoid conviction.
You quote Scripture… but resist submission.
You pray for blessing… but protect your sin.
And here’s the truth most people won’t say out loud:
Lukewarm Christianity is not safe Christianity.
It’s actually self-deception.
Jesus warned in Gospel of Matthew 7:21:
“Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.”

That means you can say the right words…
and still miss the Kingdom.

You can look clean on the outside…
and still be spiritually dying inside.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.

Because the real issue isn’t ignorance.
It’s compromise.

We don’t struggle because we don’t know.
We struggle because we don’t want to let go.

The relationship.
The habit.
The secret.
The version of life where we stay in control.
But here’s what we miss…
Jesus never asked for half.
In Gospel of Luke 9:23, He said:
“Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.”
Daily.

Not occasionally.
Not emotionally.
Not when it’s convenient.
Daily surrender.
And yes—it costs something.

It will cost your pride.
Your hidden sins.
Your need to be liked.
Your attachment to things God is asking you to release.
But what you gain?
Is everything.
Because the Gospel is not behavior modification.
It is heart transformation through Jesus Christ.
In Book of 2 Corinthians 5:17:
“If anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!”
That means you are not called to manage sin.
You are called to be made new.
And here’s the hope that changes everything—
Jesus didn’t just expose lukewarm hearts.
He pursued them.
Right after His warning, He says in Book of Revelation 3:19–20:
“Those whom I love I rebuke and discipline. So be earnest and repent. Here I am! I stand at the door and knock…”
Did you catch that?

The same Jesus who rebukes…
is the same Jesus who knocks.
This is not rejection without invitation.
This is correction with compassion.

Grace is not ignoring your sin.
Grace is confronting it… and offering you a way out.
Through the cross.
At the cross, Jesus didn’t die for a lukewarm version of you.
He died to give you a burning heart—alive, surrendered, fully His.
So this is the moment.

Not tomorrow.
Not “when you’re ready.”
Now.
Ask yourself:

Am I truly following Jesus…
or just staying close enough to feel safe?
Because there is no middle ground in the Kingdom.
It’s not about perfection.
It’s about direction.

Are you moving toward Him…
or drifting away while still wearing His name?
If this is hitting your heart, don’t ignore it.

That’s not guilt.
That’s conviction.
And conviction is a gift.
Because it means God is still calling you back.
So respond.

Repent.
Return.
Reignite.

Let today be the day your faith stops being casual…
and becomes consuming.
And remember—
He’s still knocking.
Open the door.

—
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
